subject: Onboarding stressproof playbook, benchmarks, and evidence exchange
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@everlyinc.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <legal@everlyinc.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff + initial throughput/latency targets for onboarding benchmark

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Everly is excited to move into the onboarding benchmark phase. To get us scheduled, can you confirm the acceptance targets and the artifacts you need from our side? High level asks from our infra team:

- Target baseline: handle our expected peak of ~120 req/s (single-region) with tails under control.
- Latency goals: p50 < 100 ms, p95 < 280 ms, p99 < 600 ms (these are our current internal targets; flexible if Redwood recommends adjustments).
- We'll run 30-minute sustained load runs and a few 10-minute spike tests.

We can provide sample traffic traces, a small dataset, and a service account for the test harness. If you have a short playbook or checklist we can review before the run that would help.

Can we aim for next Wednesday (6/30) for the first acceptance pass?

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
SRE Lead, Everly Inc.

P.S. attaching a quick summary of our request (everly_benchmark_request.pdf)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@everlyinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff + initial throughput/latency targets for onboarding benchmark

Hi Sam — great to see alignment after the demo. Below is our proposed "Stressproof Playbook" for Everly's onboarding benchmark. I kept it focused so your infra and ours can run the first acceptance pass next week.

1) Acceptance targets (recommended; we can tune if you prefer your internal numbers):
   - Sustained throughput: 120 req/s (single region) over 30 minutes
   - Target latency: p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 320 ms, p99 < 650 ms
   - Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx or token failures during run

2) Test matrix and cadence:
   - Warm-up: 15 min low-concurrency ramp to populate KV cache
   - Run A (sustained): 30 min at target throughput
   - Run B (spike): 3 x 10 min spikes at 200% throughput with 5 min cooldowns
   - Run C (tail stress): single long-run (60 min) with noisy short-tail sequences to exercise context handling

3) Metrics and artifacts we will collect (please share same from your side):
   - Per-request latencies (p50/p95/p99), CPU/GPU utilization, memory, queue lengths
   - Token-level breakdown, batching stats, KV cache hit ratio
   - Raw logs (aggregated), sample request/response payloads, and run-level summary CSVs

4) Test harness and data exchange:
   - We will provide a test harness that can accept your trace format; suggested schema in attached loadscript_templates.json
   - Please send a sanitized sample of real traces (first 5k requests) and a short prompt corpus (<= 2k prompts)

5) Roles/owners and timeline:
   - Redwood tech lead: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai) — will run and instrument the runtime.
   - Redwood CS owner: Chloe Martin (me) — scheduling, artifact collection, signoff coordination.
   - Everly SRE: Sam Taylor — test inputs, service accounts, and network windows.
   - Legal/procurement: Laura Chen (cc'd) for any contract/DocuSign steps.

6) Success criteria and signoff:
   - Pass: Meets latency/throughput targets and <=0.5% errors across two sustained runs.
   - Conditional pass: Misses one p95/p99 threshold but with documented mitigation (cache tuning, batch params) and agreed follow-up retest window.

Attachments: stressproof_playbook_v1.xlsx (detailed schedule), loadscript_templates.json (example harness), evidence_bundle.zip (schema for evidence upload).

If that looks good, we'll book the 6/30 slot and Ben will send the run script + a short run checklist.

Thanks — cc'ing Monica for visibility.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@everlyinc.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff + initial throughput/latency targets for onboarding benchmark

Hi team — quick technical notes to make runs deterministic and avoid noisy regressions: 

- KV cache warm-up: we should replay 15-20% of the peak traffic during warm-up with identical prefix distributions to hit realistic cache hit ratios. If Everly can provide a 5k-request sample with sequence-length distribution that matches production, that will speed things.
- Sequence length buckets: recommend tests for short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-256), and long (>256) separately — mixing them hides tail behavior.
- Concurrency control: use fixed concurrency drivers rather than open-loop rate generators for the spike tests to keep latencies meaningful. We can provide a Gatling/Locust driver wrapper.
- Quantization/variant note: we'll run on the model variant you selected; if you want a fallback quantized variant for cost tests we can include that as Run D.

I'll push the initial run script by EOD and include an instrumentation checklist: telemetry endpoints, expected log markers, and the S3 path for evidence upload.

Ben
Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <legal@everlyinc.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@everlyinc.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff + initial throughput/latency targets for onboarding benchmark

Hi all — from procurement/legal side, quick request:

- Please confirm any data retention or logging that Redwood will keep post-benchmark. Everly needs a 90-day retention window for logs related to this run, and ability to request deletion.
- We'll circulate a short NDA amendment and a DocuSign envelope for the onboarding trial terms.

Sam — can you confirm a contact for procurement so we can route the DocuSign link?

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Senior Counsel, Everly Inc.
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@everlyinc.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff + initial throughput/latency targets for onboarding benchmark

Thanks everyone — quick operational note from Redwood leadership:

- Schedule confirmed for 2027-06-30 as a tentative first pass. Ben/chloe — please lock the daily two-hour window 09:00-11:00 PT and share calendar invites with service account details.
- If the first pass is a conditional pass, we'll allow one automated retest within 72 hours without additional charges; larger rework will be scoped.
- For signoff, we require: two sustained runs passing targets, evidence bundle uploaded to our S3 path, and a short post-run readout (15-30m) where we walk through artifacts.

Appreciate the clear plan — looking forward to a smooth run.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
